correctness.rationale: Commuting permutation actions factor through Z^2 and transitivity identifies pointed structures with Z^2/L. Loop(f^u g^v) is true exactly for (u,v) in L, yielding completeness by a direct symmetric-difference separator. Column HNF gives sigma_1(d) classes and the stated divisor sum. For two different index-at-most-N lattices, generators of a strictly smaller-index lattice have L1 norm at most that index; at equal index N, the HNF case split yields generators of norm at most N-1 or a primitive vector of norm at most N-1 unique to its index-N lattice. An N-versus-(N-1) cyclic pair proves sharpness. The full relation is a bisimulation without propositions and loop. The executable independent orbit simulator checks the algebraic statements through N=20 but is not relied on for unbounded N.

value.rationale: The theorem answers an exact natural observation problem for transitive finite commuting actions: which orbit systems can proposition-free LoopPDL distinguish, and what is the smallest worst-case length of one direct return-to-state word query at a fixed world-budget? It gives a sharp linear bound in all sizes and a matching obstruction, converts logic types to subgroup data, and isolates the expressive contribution of loop. The structural two-generator condition is independently motivated by commuting programs; this is not an arbitrary computation or merely classical divisor sums.
